To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BV seed can replace up to 20% of corn in the broiler diet without adverse effects on the broiler growth performance.
feeding 100 or 200  g/kg of raw BV to broilers decreased feed intake and weight gains, and cooking BV did not improve feed intake or weight gain.

feeding 200 g BV/kg in broiler diet reduced feed intake, weight gain, and feed conversion ratio and Met supplementation of 200 g of cooked BV/kg resulted in similar feed intake, weight gains, and feed conversion ratios to the control diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of BV seeds in poultry nutrition and how it can be used as an alternative to soybean meal.
the use of BV as a feed ingredient.
the development of a practical method for the use of BV seeds in poultry feed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BV seeds are an adequate feed ingredient, provided the birds are fed with Met-supplemented diets, and the seeds are heated to improve the digestibility of the protein.
cooking and methionin supplementation of 200 g of raw bitter vetch per kg of feed is recommended for use as a feed ingredient of broiler diets.

BV seeds are not a suitable feed ingredient for broiler chickens, but if BV seeds are used, then they should be cooked and supplemented with Met to achieve a similar growth performance to the control group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BV seeds are a good protein source but the amino acid profile needs to be improved by supplementation of the Met.
the BV seeds could be used in broilers diet up to 100 g/ kg, and that the use of 200 g/ kg BV seeds would be possible if the seeds were heated and supplemented with Met.
BV seeds can replace 100 g of soybean meal/kg of diet without any negative effect, but the BV seeds should be heated before inclusion in broiler diets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BV seeds are a poor feed ingredient and that the use of BV seeds as feed ingredients for broilers should be limited to a maximum of 100 mg/kg of the total diet.
cooking BV seeds and Met supplementation is a good strategy to use BV seeds as feed ingredients in broiler diets.
BV is a promising feed ingredient that can be used in broiler diets.
